question: 0.25 g of an organic compound, on treatment with fuming nitric acid followed by AgNO3, gave 0.22 g of AgBr. The percentage of bromine in the compound is ______.
solution:
The correct answer __**37.45%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• We are given the mass of the organic compound as 0.25 g.
 
• Upon treatment and reaction with silver nitrate (AgNO3​), the bromine in the organic compound is converted to silver bromide (AgBr).
 
• The mass of silver bromide obtained is 0.22 g.
 
• To find the percentage of bromine in the organic compound, we need to determine the mass of bromine present in 0.22 g of silver bromide.
 
• The molar mass of silver (Ag) is approximately 107.87 g/mol.
 
• The molar mass of bromine (Br) is approximately 79.90 g/mol.
 
• Therefore, the molar mass of silver bromide (AgBr) is 107.87+79.90=187.77 g/mol.
 
• In one mole of silver bromide (187.77 g), the mass of bromine is 79.90 g.
 
• We can set up a proportion to find the mass of bromine in 0.22 g of silver bromide: Molar Mass of BromineMass of Bromine​=Molar Mass of Silver BromideMass of Silver Bromide​ 79.90g/molMass of Bromine​=187.77g/mol0.22g​
 
• Solving for the mass of bromine: Mass of Bromine=187.77g/mol0.22g×79.90g/mol​ Mass of Bromine≈0.0936g
 
• Now, to find the percentage of bromine in the original organic compound, we divide the mass of bromine by the mass of the organic compound and multiply by 100%: Percentage of Bromine=Mass of Organic CompoundMass of Bromine​×100% Percentage of Bromine=0.25g0.0936g​×100% Percentage of Bromine≈37.44%
 
• Looking at the given options, 37.45% is the closest value.
